output.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) requested an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and fix wrong bills after tickets doubled since August (CL-01, E-07). An initial problem definition attributed this to a field manual-read route-completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-02), but that premise was invalidated by E-12: the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills actually trace to AMI meters, not manual field reads. The successor problem (PD-1@v2) establishes the root cause as billing import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), which compares raw register values to a 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling; v4.2-firmware meters report in '0.1 m3' units versus 'm3' for older firmware (E-14), causing normal reads to be misflagged as high consumption and rejected. E-15 confirmed the 1184 rejected bills are predominantly v4.2 firmware, resolving the deferred unknown U-FIRMWARE-REJECTION-LINK. This explains only the ESTIMATED-read minority (1240 of 3025 disputed bills); the larger ACTUAL-read majority (1785/3025, E-01) remains unexplained. The release delivers the sole in-scope item from SD-2: flagging the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills for Billing Operations manual review (work item W-EXEC-FLAG-ESTIMATE-BILLS, status DONE), with no automated writes to customer bills, consistent with the K-BILLWRITE authority constraint. The decision recorded is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds, following a DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS and a documented list of unresolved items filed as known limitations rather than release blockers.
